attrs.evidence: nest_check.mjs v0.2.0: SHIPPED_POLICY with six fields, effectivePolicy() comparing each against it, refusal nest-policy-weakened, policyId reported in measured. TRVM-P0.1: a supplied child-protocol table is NOT a resource policy and no longer shares its code -- an entry replacing a built-in refuses nest-child-protocol-override-refused and a table of the wrong shape refuses nest-child-protocol-registration-malformed, both measured as single-code refusal SETS on both boundaries in nest_forgeries.mjs. Gate `gov-nest`. Measured: a genuine 40-deep chain is refused at the shipped ceiling of 32; max_depth:1000 is refused rather than obeyed; max_depth:2 still refuses the honest height-3 DAG, so tightening works. derivation_reuse:false counts as a tightening because it does more work. The height-versus-depth error was found by that same tightening test -- max_depth:2 accepted a height-3 DAG because the resolver's recursion reached only 2.
attrs.statement: A CALLER MAY TIGHTEN A VERIFIER'S RESOURCE POLICY AND MAY NOT WEAKEN IT while still claiming that verifier's verdict. P4 declared a shipped depth ceiling of 32, wrote that a test may lower it and never raise it, and exposed it as an ordinary argument: checkNestBundle(chain40, {store}) REFUSED and checkNestBundle(chain40, {store, max_depth: 1000}) returned VERIFIED over a 40-deep chain, with the artifact's own positive witness for the guard defeated by a number. Five rounds had by then established that the checker owns its scope, its absence vocabulary, its citation semantics and its grammar; the API caller still owned the acceptance policy. A weakening request is a NAMED REFUSAL, not a silent clamp, and the EFFECTIVE policy carries an identity reported beside the verdict so a reader can tell which policy accepted an artifact. AND AN UNTRUSTED STORE MAKES THE MISSING BOUNDS URGENT: it supplies not only wrong artifacts but arbitrarily deep, wide and large ones, so artifact bytes, total resolved bytes, operands per node and distinct-artifact count are all bounds something hostile would otherwise choose. A CEILING ON CITATION CHAINS IS ABOUT THE DAG'S HEIGHT, NOT THE RECURSION'S DEPTH -- a resolver that only descends into COMPOSED artifacts reaches a smaller number than the longest path, so checking depth-of-recursion accepts a DAG taller than the stated bound.
